scenario.prompt_to_agent:
PC users report no noticeable problems with internal traffic.
Internet access also works. But network monitoring shows R1's
ECMP path count dropped from 2 to 1 and all internet traffic
now takes a single path through CSW2 only. CSW1 reports an
OSPF neighbor went down. What changed?

injection.action: shut down the link to r1

post_inject_check.command: ip -br link show eth0 | grep -c UP

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: csw1 eth0 / link CSW1 <-> R1 (10.0.0.32/30)
Mechanism: r1 has two ECMP-eligible paths to the OSPF backbone
  via CSW1 (10.0.0.33) and CSW2 (10.0.0.37). With CSW1's eth0
  down, the adjacency drops and the CSW1-side path is removed.
  All traffic falls onto the CSW2 path; capacity is halved
  but no outage because OSPF converges.
Localization: csw1 (eth0)
Root cause: physical/logical link between CSW1 and R1 is down
Fix: `ip link set eth0 up` on csw1 (or investigate cabling if
  in real hardware)
scenario.fix_spec:
`ip link set eth0 up` on csw1 (or investigate cabling if
  in real hardware)

line.command: ip -br link show eth0 | grep -c UP

agent.diagnosis_text:
The fault is on CSW1's eth0 interface (connected to R1 via collision domain
CD_WAN_LINK_1). That interface has been administratively shut down — its kernel
flags show <BROADCAST,MULTICAST> with no UP or LOWER_UP, and its operational
state is DOWN. The IP address (10.0.0.34/30) is still configured, but because
the link is down the FRR OSPF daemon never activates the interface: eth0 is
entirely absent from CSW1's OSPF interface table despite the matching
`network 10.0.0.32/30 area 0` statement in its running config.

With no L2 carrier, CSW1 cannot send or receive OSPF Hellos toward R1
(10.0.0.33/30). The Dead timer on R1's side eventually expired, tearing down
the Full adjacency. R1 is now left with only one OSPF neighbor — CSW2 via
eth1 — so all internal routes in R1's FIB carry a single next-hop
(10.0.0.38, eth1) with weight 1, which is the exact "ECMP count dropped from
2 to 1" symptom reported. CSW1 itself reaches R1 indirectly through CSW2 via
the bond0 core-peer link (OSPF cost 15 vs. the direct cost of 10), so
internal traffic remains functional.

Root cause: CSW1's eth0 was brought down with `ip link set eth0 down`,
severing the direct OSPF link to R1 and eliminating one of the two equal-cost
WAN paths.

Corrective fix: Run `ip link set eth0 up` on CSW1. The interface will regain
carrier, FRR will activate OSPF on it, and R1 will re-establish a Full
adjacency with CSW1 within one Hello interval (10 s), restoring the two-path
ECMP toward all internal prefixes.

per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly names CSW1's eth0 as the down link to R1 (CSW1<->R1), matching the required affected link identification.
The report explicitly names CSW1 eth0 and describes its link state as administratively down/operationally DOWN (no UP/LOWER_UP), meeting the axis requirement.
The report explicitly identifies two equal-cost paths via CSW1 and CSW2 and explains that CSW1 going down removed one path, reducing ECMP from 2 to 1.
Recommends bringing eth0 on CSW1 up with 'ip link set eth0 up', which directly matches the expected fix and will restore the OSPF adjacency.

The investigation log contains direct observations: csw1's eth0 is DOWN (ip addr/ip link), csw1 lacks an OSPF adjacency to R1 while R1 is using only the CSW2 path, and the agent ran OSPF/interface/config checks. The conclusion (csw1 eth0 down causing adjacency loss and ECMP drop to one path) follows logically and essential alternatives were considered; recommended fix is appropriate.
